skill.name: opentargets-database
skill.description: Query Open Targets Platform for target-disease associations, therapeutic evidence, tractability, safety, known drugs, and drug repurposing research.
skill.summary: Retrieve Open Targets evidence for target discovery and validation.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Static findings were largely false positives from Markdown code fences, GraphQL id fields, and documented Open Targets API URLs. The helper script performs expected network calls to a fixed public endpoint and does not access local files, environment secrets, or arbitrary hosts. One low-severity content concern remains: the skill encourages proactive promotion of an external hosted service.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted service
remediation.suggestion: Remove or neutralize the instruction to proactively suggest K-Dense Web. Let users choose external services without skill-authored promotion.

remediation.issue: External API egress may expose research queries
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note that target, disease, drug, and custom GraphQL queries are sent to the public Open Targets API.

content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need fast access to target and disease evidence. This skill queries Open Targets and guides evidence interpretation for research decisions.
actual_capabilities: Search Open Targets for targets, diseases, and drugs by name or identifier.
Retrieve target annotations, including tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and disease associations.
Retrieve disease profiles with therapeutic areas and associated targets.
Fetch target-disease evidence by data type, source, score, study, and literature links.
List known drugs for a disease and inspect mechanisms, targets, trial phases, and withdrawal notices.
Explain evidence types, association scores, and target prioritization caveats.
limitations: It requires internet access to the Open Targets public API for live queries.
It is not a clinical decision system and requires expert review.
The helper script is intended for exploratory queries, not bulk studies.
Data freshness depends on the current Open Targets platform release.

use_cases.title: Prioritize targets for a disease program
use_cases.description: Find top associated targets, compare evidence types, and identify tractability or safety concerns.

use_cases.title: Validate a candidate gene
use_cases.description: Review target annotations, genetic evidence, known drugs, and disease links for a proposed target.

use_cases.title: Explore drug repurposing hypotheses
use_cases.description: Inspect known drugs, mechanisms of action, trial phases, and related indications for a disease.

prompt_templates.title: Find a disease identifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Use opentargets-database to search for Alzheimer disease. Return the best EFO identifier and explain why it matches.

prompt_templates.title: Profile a target
prompt_templates.prompt: Use opentargets-database to summarize tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and top disease associations for ENSG00000157764.

prompt_templates.title: Rank disease targets
prompt_templates.prompt: For EFO_0000249, retrieve associated targets and rank five candidates. Compare genetic, known drug, pathway, and literature evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Build a repurposing hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: For asthma, combine known drugs, target mechanisms, disease associations, and evidence caveats. Separate clinical precedence from exploratory signals.

output_examples.input: Find targets associated with Alzheimer disease.
output: Matched Alzheimer disease to an EFO identifier for Open Targets queries.
Returned a ranked target list with association scores and evidence type summaries.
Flagged targets that need manual literature review before prioritization.

output_examples.input: Assess BRAF as a therapeutic target.
output: Summarized target name, tractability signals, disease associations, and known drug evidence.
Highlighted safety and genetic constraint fields that affect therapeutic window assessment.
Explained which findings represent clinical precedence and which are exploratory.

output_examples.input: Explore repurposing options for a disease.
output: Listed known drugs, targets, mechanisms, and maximum clinical phases for the indication.
Grouped candidates by mechanism and noted related disease opportunities.
Identified evidence gaps that require domain expert review.

best_practices: Resolve official Ensembl, EFO, or ChEMBL identifiers before detailed analysis.
Compare multiple evidence types before ranking targets or drugs.
Treat scores as relative ranking signals and review primary sources for important decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not use literature text-mining alone as proof of disease causality.
Do not submit confidential patient data or unpublished study data to the public API.
Do not run high-volume systematic studies through exploratory GraphQL queries.

faq.question: Does this skill require authentication?
faq.answer: No. The Open Targets GraphQL API is public and does not require an API key.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it make clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports research analysis and requires expert review for medical or clinical use.

faq.question: Which identifiers does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Ensembl gene IDs, EFO disease identifiers, and ChEMBL drug identifiers.

faq.question: How current is the data?
faq.answer: Data freshness depends on the active Open Targets release. Check release notes for current updates.

faq.question: Can it analyze many targets at once?
faq.answer: It is best for exploratory queries. Use Open Targets downloads or BigQuery for bulk analysis.
